title: How Error Account 88888 Destroyed 233-Year-Old Barings Bank
alt_title_1: Nick Leeson's $1.4B Collapse: Never Audit Your Own Bets
alt_title_2: Why Mixing Execution and Accounting Bankrupted Barings in 1995
description_hook: In February 1995, 28-year-old Singapore derivatives trader Nick Leeson collapsed 233-year-old Barings Bank after hiding 827 million pounds ($1.4 billion) of unauthorized Nikkei losses inside error account 88888 because managers let him run both trading and settlement.

scenes.headline: One Hidden Account Wiped Out a 233-Year Bank
bullets: Founded in 1762 as Britain's oldest merchant bank
28-year-old Nick Leeson hid losses in error account 88888
scenes.narration: In February 1995, a twenty-eight-year-old trader in Singapore bankrupted Barings Bank, Britain's oldest merchant bank founded in 1762, using one hidden error account numbered five eights.
scenes.source: Bank of England Board of Banking Supervision, Barings Report (July 18, 1995)

scenes.headline: 827 Million Pounds Lost, Sold for 1 Pound
scenes.stat_label: FINAL SALE PRICE AFTER $1.4B NIKKEI WIPEOUT
bullets: London let Leeson run both trading and back-office settlement
Jan 1995 Kobe earthquake blew hidden losses to 827M pounds
scenes.narration: London executives let Nick Leeson run both the trading floor and back-office settlement, allowing him to conceal unauthorized Nikkei futures losses inside account 88888 until the January 1995 Kobe earthquake pushed losses to eight hundred twenty-seven million pounds, and Barings sold for one pound.
scenes.source: Bank of England Board of Banking Supervision, Barings Report (July 18, 1995)

scenes.headline: Never Let the Trader Grade the Ledger
scenes.left_body: Same impulse places bets & edits rules -> hides losses & doubles down
scenes.right_body: Hard position limits + separate cold audit -> caps mistakes early
scenes.narration: Solo investors and founders recreate that fatal structural flaw whenever the same excited brain placing a bet also grades the scorecard, moving goalposts and averaging down instead of booking a small loss.
scenes.source: Bank of England Board of Banking Supervision, Barings Report (July 18, 1995)

scenes.headline: Split Your Promoter Brain From Your Auditor Brain
scenes.stat_label: SEGREGATED RISK GATES PROTECT LONG-TERM CAPITAL
scenes.stat_subtext: Pre-set max loss + cold weekly audit -> zero ruin
scenes.narration: Separate execution from accounting: lock in hard position caps, automated stop rules, and read-only spending limits before capital goes live, then review every number during a cold Friday audit.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Bank of England Barings Report (1995)

scenes.headline: Two Centuries Vanish Without Hard Guardrails
scenes.stat_label: NEVER AUDIT A BET IN THE SAME SESSION YOU PLACE IT
bullets: Write maximum loss rules in ink before entering any trade
Audit performance on a separate day with zero ego
scenes.narration: Never let your inner promoter audit its own trades, because two centuries of compounding vanish fast without independent guardrails.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Bank of England Barings Report (1995)
